howItWorks.reviews.title: How reviews work
howItWorks.reviews.intro: A review appears on a profile, and counts towards its rating, only when all four of these are true:
howItWorks.reviews.session: It comes from a student or parent who had a session with that tutor or counselor.
howItWorks.reviews.confirm: The tutor or counselor has confirmed that the session took place.
howItWorks.reviews.approve: The Tutorcat team has checked and approved it.
howItWorks.reviews.permission: The reviewer gave permission to show it publicly.
howItWorks.reviews.records: Where a profile says “Rating shown from Tutorcat records”, the rating comes from Tutorcat’s own records, not from individual public reviews.
page.guidelines.title: Community guidelines
page.guidelines.description: What Tutorcat expects from tutors, counselors and families, and what counts as unprofessional behaviour.
guidelines.intro: Tutorcat works when families and specialists can trust each other. These guidelines apply to everyone who uses the site.
guidelines.draft: Draft, pending review by the Tutorcat team. The wording may change before it’s final.
guidelines.specialists.title: Tutors and counselors
guidelines.specialists.honest: Describe your qualifications, experience and results honestly. Never claim a permit, degree or result you don’t have.
guidelines.specialists.punctual: Arrive on time and prepared, and give fair notice if you need to cancel or reschedule.
guidelines.specialists.professional: Keep every message and session professional, respectful and about learning.
guidelines.specialists.parents: For students under 18, keep parents or guardians informed and agree lesson arrangements with them.
guidelines.specialists.boundaries: Keep contact to the channels and times you agreed. Don’t contact students privately on social media.
guidelines.specialists.privacy: Keep students’ and families’ personal details private and use them only for lessons.
guidelines.specialists.promises: Don’t guarantee grades or university admissions.
guidelines.specialists.reviews: Never write, buy or pressure anyone into a review, and never offer anything in exchange for one.
guidelines.families.title: Families and students
guidelines.families.respect: Treat tutors and counselors with courtesy and respect their time.
guidelines.families.honest: Only review sessions that really happened, and describe them honestly.
guidelines.families.arrange: Agree times, fees and cancellations with the tutor or counselor before lessons start.
guidelines.families.safety: If something feels wrong, tell us. You don’t need proof to raise a concern.
guidelines.unprofessional.title: What counts as unprofessional
guidelines.unprofessional.contact: Inappropriate messages or contact, including personal or romantic messages to a student.
guidelines.unprofessional.harassment: Harassment, discrimination or abusive language of any kind.
guidelines.unprofessional.pressure: Pressuring a family to book more lessons, pay in advance or leave a review.
guidelines.unprofessional.credentials: False credentials, fake permits or misleading claims about experience or results.
guidelines.unprofessional.payments: Asking for unusual payments, personal loans or sensitive personal information.
guidelines.concern.title: If something goes wrong
guidelines.concern.body: Contact the Tutorcat team. Concerns about a child’s safety are always handled first, and we never tell the person you report who raised the concern.

join.faq.title: Questions you might have
join.faq.tutor.cost.q: Does it cost anything to join?
join.faq.tutor.cost.a: The first {count} tutors list free for good, with a boosted profile included. After that, a listing will cost $1 a month, or $3 for a boosted listing, billed yearly. Nothing is charged today.
join.faq.tutor.contact.q: Will families see my email or phone number?
join.faq.tutor.contact.a: No. Your email, phone and social profiles stay private. Families send an introduction request through Tutorcat, and we put you in touch.
join.faq.tutor.permit.q: How do I get the “Permit verified” badge?
join.faq.tutor.permit.a: For now it’s available to tutors in the UAE. Send us your MoHRE Private Teacher Work Permit and our team will check it before the badge appears.
join.faq.tutor.payments.q: How are lessons and payments arranged?
join.faq.tutor.payments.a: You agree times and fees directly with each family. Tutorcat doesn’t take payments for lessons.
join.faq.tutor.both.q: I tutor and counsel. Do I need two profiles?
join.faq.tutor.both.a: No. Choose “Tutor + Counselor” in the form and you’ll have one profile that shows both.
join.faq.tutor.review.a: Your form opens as an email to the Tutorcat team. We review every application before listing anyone, and we’ll email you if we need more information.
join.faq.counselor.cost.q: Does it cost anything to join?
join.faq.counselor.cost.a: The first {count} counselors list free for good, with a boosted profile included. After that, a listing will cost $1 a month, or $3 for a boosted listing, billed yearly. Nothing is charged today.
join.faq.counselor.contact.q: Will families see my email or phone number?
join.faq.counselor.contact.a: No. Your email, phone and social profiles stay private. Families send an introduction request through Tutorcat, and we put you in touch.
join.faq.counselor.experience.q: Do I need to have studied where I advise?
join.faq.counselor.experience.a: Families value first-hand experience, so tell us where you studied or worked. Your profile lists the destinations you advise on and where you studied.
join.faq.counselor.commission.q: Do I have to tell you about commissions?
join.faq.counselor.commission.a: Yes. If universities or agents pay you commissions or referral fees, you must tell us when you apply.
join.faq.counselor.both.q: I counsel and tutor. Do I need two profiles?
join.faq.counselor.both.a: No. Choose “Tutor + Counselor” in the form and you’ll have one profile that shows both.
join.faq.counselor.review.a: Your form opens as an email to the Tutorcat team. We review every application before listing anyone, and we’ll email you if we need more information.
join.bothNote: Tutor and counselor? Choose “Tutor + Counselor” in the form for one profile that shows both.
page.report.title: Report a concern
page.report.description: Tell the Tutorcat team about a tutor, counselor, review or message that worries you. Concerns about a child’s safety are handled first.
report.intro: Something about a tutor, a counselor, a review or a message worries you? Tell us here. Reports are never published.
report.urgent.title: If someone is in danger right now
report.urgent.body: Contact your local emergency services first, then tell us. This form opens an email to our team, and that inbox isn’t watched around the clock.
report.aboutDetails: Their name, or where you came across them (optional)
report.category.childSafety: A concern about a child’s safety
report.childSafetyNote: We’ll mark this report URGENT so the team sees it first. If a child is in danger right now, contact emergency services first.
report.contactType.messages: In messages (WhatsApp, text, email or social media)
report.descriptionPlaceholder: In your own words: what was said or done, and by whom.
report.name: Your name
report.contact: Email or phone, if you’d like us to follow up
report.anonymous: Leave both blank to report without your details; we then can’t follow up with you. Your email app still shows us the address you send the report from.
report.screenshots: Screenshots help. Attach them in your email app before you press send; this page can’t upload files.
report.consent: This is true to the best of my knowledge, and Tutorcat may use it to look into the concern.
report.reference: Your reference is {reference}. It’s in the email subject, so you can quote it if you write to us again.
report.next.title: What happens next
report.next.send: Your email app opens a draft addressed to the Tutorcat team. Nothing is sent until you press send.
report.next.read: The team reads every report. Concerns about a child’s safety are handled first.
report.next.followUp: If you included your contact details, we may get in touch to ask for more information.
report.next.profile: We may hide a profile while we look into a concern.
report.next.private: Reports are never published, and we don’t tell the person you report who raised the concern.
